newsitem.title: SPAIN: ETA claims responsibility for Spain killings.
newsitem.headline: ETA claims responsibility for Spain killings.

text.p: The Basque separatist guerrilla group ETA has claimed responsibility for five attacks in Spain in recent months including the assassination of a Supreme Court judge.
ETA, which had already been blamed by the Spanish government for the killings, made the claim in a communique sent late Wednesday night to news organisations in the northern Basque region.

ETA has killed about 800 people in a 29-year battle for an independent Basque state encompassing parts of northern Spain and southern France. The group stepped up attacks this year, killing seven people so far, after a relative lull in the violence 1996.

The statement said ETA, which stands for Basque Homeland and Freedom, was behind the assassination of Supreme Court Judge Rafael Martinez Emperador, shot in the head outside his Madrid home on February 10.

On the same day, the group said it set off a car bomb in the southern city of Granada which killed hairdresser Domingo Puente Marin, who was passing in an army vehicle on his way to work at a nearby military base.
ETA said one of its gunmen killed Basque businessman Patxi Arratibel the next day in the town of Tolosa in Guipuzcoa province.
Basque police said Arratibel, who was also shot in the head, had acted as an intermediary in negotiations between ETA and family members in the 1988 kidnapping of businessman Emiliano Revilla.
Arratibel was convicted in 1994 for having illegal contacts with ETA and was sentenced to two years probation. ETA later accused him of keeping part of the ransom money.
ETA said it planted an explosive device on February 17 under the car of national policeman Modesto Rico Pasarin in the Basque commercial centre of Bilbao. He died in the explosion.

The group also claimed responsibility for killing prison psychologist Francisco Javier Gomez Elosegui on March 11 in San Sebastian. One of the gunmen involved in the attack, Fernando Elejalde, was caught by police as he fled the site of the shooting.
